G1; MINOR; Executed credit agreement, indentures, supplemental indentures and guarantees are not supplied and none is declared. Covenant tests, the revolver springing-maturity conditions and guarantee release terms are known only from the company's descriptions.; Covenant, priority and recovery statements can be no better than the filing summaries; the 2030 revolver maturity cannot be tested against its springing condition.; Searched every source for the springing-maturity conditions: each repeats the reference to the credit agreement without stating them. The exhibit list names the financing documents as filed exhibits only.; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 116–118; Supply the credit agreement, amendments and indentures; until then label every covenant statement as a company summary.

G2; MINOR; Management net debt and net leverage at 2025-12-31 and the 2025 results release filed on 2026-02-26 are not supplied. The 2026 releases print net leverage only at 2026-03-31, 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30.; A year-end 2025 leverage figure quoted by the Financial foundation has no management figure to compare with; 2025 Adjusted EBITDA is available only through the annual report reconciliation and the release reconciliations.; Searched all seven sources for net debt and net leverage near the 2025 year end: only covenant references and the three 2026 quarter-end figures were found.; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86; Supply the 2025 results release, or state the year-end management figure as not established.

G3; MINOR; No filing after the annual report prints a debt maturity schedule. The annual report schedule shows term loans due in 2028, but the March 2026 amendment moved them to March 2031.; The maturity wall at 2026-09-30 must be rebuilt from the amended term loan terms, so nearest-maturity and refinancing-window statements are derived values.; Searched the three quarterly reports and the 2026 releases for maturity tables (maturities, thereafter, contractual obligations): none found; the quarterly market-risk item refers back to the annual report.; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 104–105; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 155; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59; Rebuild the schedule from the Q3 term loan note and label it derived.

G4; MINOR; The 2026 proxy statement and the subsidiary list are not supplied. Items 10 to 14 of the annual report are incorporated by reference to the proxy statement, and the only sponsor voting power figure predates the August 2026 secondary offering.; Board independence, committees, pay, related-party detail, current sponsor ownership and the full guarantor map cannot be established; governance conclusions rest on officer biographies, controlled-company text and risk factors.; Searched the annual report Part III and exhibit list, and all three quarterly reports for voting power and beneficial ownership: no current figure found.; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 115; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 120; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; Supply the proxy statement and exhibit 21.1, or label ownership and governance statements as of the annual report date.

G5; MINOR; Periods are not like for like. 2023 reflects only BlueTriton, Primo Water is included from 2024-11-09, remaining international businesses are in discontinued operations, the auditor changed after 2023 and the releases revised the presentation of 2025 comparable net sales.; Growth and margin comparisons across 2023, 2024 and 2025 mix different scopes; 2026 growth against 2025 needs the exited-business adjustments the releases print.; Stated in the sources; no search needed.; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 125; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 13; Keep each period separate and label each comparison with its scope.

G6; MINOR; Three different debt totals appear at 2026-09-30: balance sheet debt of USD 5,162.1 million, net of unamortized costs and, on the annual report's year-end presentation, including finance leases; principal of USD 5,249.7 million before unamortized costs used for management net leverage; and USD 5,017.5 million in the fair-value table, which covers term loans and notes only.; Using one total for leverage and another for interest cover mixes perimeters and changes the ratio.; Stated in the sources; compared across the three tables.; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92; The Financial foundation should name the perimeter it uses and keep each total separate.

facts.label: Leverage and coverage
facts.text: Net debt on reported EBITDA fell from 4.51x at 2026-03-31 to 3.87x at 2026-09-30, but the move came from earnings and cash, not repayment: last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose by USD 130.4 million while gross debt rose by USD 6.8 million, and USD 111.0 million of the EBITDA rise is lower acquisition, integration and restructuring costs in the second and third quarters than a year earlier. - The filings print a dash, which means nothing was reported, in 7 income statement cells, 36 cash flow cells and 3 balance sheet cells; each is written as not supplied rather than zero. No ratio uses these cells, so nothing is restricted. Severity Low. No action is needed unless the issuer confirms that a dash means nil. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 126–128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–7 - The annual report and the quarterly reports print different line sets, so 6 income statement cells, 78 cash flow cells and 9 balance sheet cells are not printed in the filing for that column; for example proceeds from the sale of property, plant and equipment become a separate line only from the second quarter of 2026 and the 2024 financing items do not recur. This limits line-by-line comparison across columns and nothing else. Severity Low. The action is to compare the subtotals, which are printed in every column. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_prmb-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-03-31_prmb-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 5 - Net Cash Change is withheld for FY2024, FY2025 and the first quarter, half year and nine months of 2025 because the printed net change includes the cash flows of discontinued operations, which the three activity rows exclude; the printed net change stays in the issuer's own row. This restricts only the cash roll-forward check for 2025. Severity Low. The action is to read the discontinued operations rows beside it. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 127–128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7 - No filing after the annual report prints a debt maturity schedule, so the maturity chart is drawn at 2025-12-31 and still shows USD 3,005.7 million of term loans in 2028 that were extended to March 2031 on 2026-03-31. This restricts any maturity wall or refinancing-window statement as at the cutoff. Severity Medium. The action is to rebuild the post-amendment schedule from the term loan terms and label it derived. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 104–105; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 155; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59 - Instrument-level carrying values, finance leases, other debt and the total of unamortized costs are not stated at 2026-09-30, so the debt instruments register cannot reconcile to balance sheet debt and a gap of USD 144.6 million to the fair-value table stays unitemised; the year-end reconciliation is complete. This restricts instrument-level leverage and secured-debt statements at the cutoff. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the quarter's debt note or the issuer's schedule. Basis: calculation C59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92 - Management net debt and net leverage at 2025-12-31 are not printed in any source read, because the 2025 results release that carries them is not supplied; the three 2026 quarter-end figures are. This restricts a comparison of year-end leverage with management's own figure. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the 2025 results release. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86 - The credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so covenant definitions, any springing conditions on the revolver, and headroom against the first lien net leverage limit of 5.00 to 1.00 and the interest coverage minimum of 2.00 to 1.00 are not calculable; the issuer reports compliance only. This restricts any covenant or maturity-condition conclusion. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the executed agreements. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 95–96 - The issuer does not state whether each add-back in Adjusted EBITDA is realised, and the bridge amounts reconcile exactly but their classification beyond the issuer's labels is not given. This restricts how far adjusted leverage can be relied on. Severity Medium. The action is to treat the add-backs as unverified and to seek the issuer's classification. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12 - Ranking is not stated for finance leases, other debt or the non-tendered original notes, and the revolver's security is stated only through the credit agreement description, so the first three are left out of the debt stack and the revolver is shown with that caveat. This restricts structural-priority statements. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the guarantee and security documents. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 95; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 98; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 161 - The dividend declared on 2026-11-03 has no stated total, so the cash figure uses the share count of that date; the record-date count may differ. This restricts the pro forma net debt row slightly. Severity Low. The action is to replace it with the paid amount once reported. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39 - The 2025-09-30 balance sheet is not in a supplied filing, so no 2025 interim balance is shown beside the 2026 interim balances. This restricts the year-on-year comparison of debt and cash at interim dates. Severity Low. The action is none unless a third-quarter 2025 filing is added. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4 - Per-share data and share counts are not carried in the statement tables, because no credit metric uses them, and the single reporting segment means no segment schedule exists; revenue by water type is in the KPI dashboard instead. This restricts nothing in the ratios. Severity Low. No action is needed. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a payout-risk view is that the sponsor may still hold at least 30%, because the 32.0% figure is rounded and the August 2026 shares may not all have come from the group; if so, the consent rights survive. Payouts also look affordable in 2026 at 62.98% of free cash flow, net leverage has fallen to 3.32x, the only distribution made to the sponsor alone, USD 448.6 million, pre-dates the merger, and none of the 2025 or 2026 refinancings is described as a priming, uptier or drop-down. facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The 2025 refinancing replaced several instruments in one programme. Exchange offers for the three senior note series drew participation of 99.97%, 98.20% and 99.53%, and the new notes are co-issued by Primo Water Holdings Inc. and Triton Water Holdings, Inc. and guaranteed by the parent and substantially all material wholly owned domestic subsidiaries. On 2025-02-12 the Fourth Amendment repriced the term loans of USD 3,098.6 million principal and added a USD 750.0 million revolver maturing in February 2030, while a USD 350.0 million asset-based facility and Primo Water's prior revolver, which had an initial USD 350.0 million commitment, were repaid and ended. The new secured notes share the term loans' first lien and the 2029 unsecured notes rank below them; holders of original notes who did not tender lost most covenants on all three series and their guarantees on the two secured series, and USD 12.9 million of those notes remains. facts.label: Business model and credit linkage
facts.text: Primo Brands sells branded spring, purified, premium and refill water through retail, Direct Delivery, Exchange and Refill, formats that combine consumer retail demand with a recurring delivery and refill base. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is high: national and regional beverage companies, retailer private labels and tap-water alternatives compete on brand, price and distribution, which limits price increases. New entry is limited by the cost of replicating a spring-source and depot network, which management calls difficult to replicate, while substitutes, from filtration to municipal water, cap the premium for bottled water. Buyer power is high because retail is consolidated and one customer is 21% of net sales, and supplier power is moderate because some packaging inputs come from few or sole suppliers; the credit effect is a margin ceiling that makes cost pass-through slower than cost inflation. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Primo Brands presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, brands and a spring-source network, but credit quality is constrained by leverage that rests on add-backs, margin pressure in 2026 and a payout policy that the sponsor's falling stake no longer checks. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow rose to USD 319.6 million in nine months and interest cover is 4.05x, though adjusted free cash flow overstates it by USD 283.3 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA recovery and on payouts staying below free cash flow before the 2028 euro notes fall due on 2028-10-31, and the primary downside path is cost inflation and service disruption lowering EBITDA while payouts continue. Further analysis would require a printed maturity schedule, covenant definitions, the sponsor's current holding and fourth-quarter results. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: shareholder payouts outpacing free cash flow while margin pressure persists. Basis: calculation C04; calculation C08; calculation C16; calculation C10; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Top risk: shareholder payouts outpacing free cash flow while margin pressure persists.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and releases are enough to support a creditor snapshot of Primo Brands Corp as of 2026-11-05, with covenant, legal-priority and governance conclusions limited by the absence of executed financing documents and the proxy statement. Creditors should treat any such conclusion as resting on the company's own summaries of its debt agreements, not on the agreements themselves.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 115–118; calculation C01

Coverage runs from the audited 2025 annual report to the third-quarter 2026 report and release published on the as-of date, so the latest balance sheet is dated 2026-09-30. The main source limits are the missing management-reported net leverage at the 2025 year end, a debt maturity schedule that predates the March 2026 term loan refinancing, and earlier history that is not comparable because the 2023 results reflect only one of the two businesses merged in 2024.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage is falling but stays high, helped more by fading one-off costs and a cash build than by repayment: net debt was 3.87x reported last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-09-30 against 4.42x at the 2025 year end. Gross debt is flat at USD 5,162.1 million and liquidity is USD 1,064.0 million of cash and undrawn revolver.
Basis: calculation C70; calculation C67; calculation C05; calculation C26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51

Creditors should anchor on reported EBITDA rather than management's 3.32x, which uses adjusted EBITDA and principal: USD 227.0 million of add-backs separate the two measures, the issuer states no realisation status for them, and the covenant definitions are not supplied. The term loans now run to 2031, so the next large maturities are the 2028 and 2029 notes.

### Leverage and coverage

Net debt on reported EBITDA fell from 4.51x at 2026-03-31 to 3.87x at 2026-09-30, but the move came from earnings and cash, not repayment: last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose by USD 130.4 million while gross debt rose by USD 6.8 million, and USD 111.0 million of the EBITDA rise is lower acquisition, integration and restructuring costs in the second and third quarters than a year earlier. Creditors should read the improvement as the roll-off of integration costs plus a cash build of USD 189.2 million since March, which holds only if free cash flow keeps going to cash rather than shareholders.
Basis: calculation C68; calculation C70; calculation C55; calculation C57; calculation C63; calculation C54; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 11

On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA the same net debt is 3.26x, and management reports 3.32x because it measures principal less unrestricted cash; the USD 227.0 million of add-backs between the two EBITDA measures is the main interpretive risk, since the issuer states no realisation status for them and reported EBITDA itself includes unrealized commodity and currency gains of USD 39.7 million in the first nine months of 2026. A creditor that underwrites to adjusted EBITDA is relying on acquisition, integration and restructuring add-backs of USD 271.8 million in 2025 and USD 91.2 million in the first nine months of 2026.
Basis: calculation C73; calculation C60; calculation C76; calculation C37; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 11–14; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86

Reported EBITDA covers cash interest 4.05x over the twelve months to 2026-09-30 against 3.57x for 2025, with cash interest USD 20.2 million below the accrued expense; the March 2026 amendment raised the term loan margin by 0.50 percentage points, which adds about USD 15.4 million a year at the current balance, so part of the cover gain from earnings is given back.
Basis: calculation C74; calculation C72; calculation C62; calculation C65; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 156
### Cash flow quality

Free cash flow after capital expenditure was USD 319.6 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 203.4 million a year earlier, on operating cash flow of USD 625.3 million against USD 477.2 million; dividends and repurchases took USD 201.3 million, or 62.98% of free cash flow, and the board approved a new repurchase program of up to USD 300.0 million on 2026-11-03. With gross debt flat, free cash flow is funding cash and shareholder returns rather than debt reduction, so further deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth.
Basis: calculation C51; calculation C50; calculation C52; calculation C53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39

Working capital absorbed USD 163.5 million in trade receivables and released USD 135.3 million through payables and accruals in the first nine months of 2026, so operating cash flow leans on payables timing; capital expenditure was 5.83% of net sales against 6.52% for 2025, and the issuer does not split maintenance from growth capital.
### Liquidity and refinancing

Cash and the undrawn revolver total USD 1,064.0 million at 2026-09-30, made up of USD 477.4 million of cash and USD 586.6 million of revolver availability after USD 163.4 million of letters of credit; no committed facility is stated to expire within twelve months, and the current portion of debt is USD 74.4 million. The revolver's February 2030 maturity carries a springing condition that the filings do not print, so liquidity beyond the 2028 and 2029 notes cannot be tested against it.
Basis: calculation C26; calculation C24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51

The March 2026 amendment moved the term loans of USD 3,090.0 million from March 2028 to March 2031, so the next large maturities are the 3.875% euro notes due 2028-10-31 and the 4.375% and 6.250% notes due 2029-04-30 and 2029-04-01, USD 1,930.1 million together at carrying value. The maturity chart is drawn at the 2025 year end because no later schedule is printed, so its 2028 column still includes USD 3,005.7 million of term loans that have since been extended; creditors should read the true 2028 maturity as the euro notes plus small other debt.
### Subsequent events and one-off items

On 2026-11-03 the board declared a dividend of 0.12 USD per share payable on 2026-12-04, which on the 2026-11-03 share count needs about USD 43.4 million; pro forma net debt is USD 4,728.1 million and pro forma net leverage 3.91x, and the new repurchase program of up to USD 300.0 million changes net debt only when shares are bought. The cash leaves after the cutoff and is not in any period figure.
Basis: calculation C40; calculation C41; calculation C42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

The term loan amendment cost USD 17.7 million of loss on modification and extinguishment in the first nine months of 2026, 2025 reported EBITDA included USD 47.3 million of insurance proceeds that the issuer deducts in adjusted EBITDA, and other operating income of USD 45.7 million in the first nine months of 2026 is the unrealized gain that the issuer also removes; each is in the income statement and the bridge with its source.

Claims outside the debt figure are operating lease obligations of USD 612.1 million on the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, purchase obligations of USD 187.1 million and a postretirement benefit obligation of USD 7.7 million at 2025-12-31, USD 163.4 million of letters of credit, and securities and consumer litigation for which no loss is accrued or estimated. Creditors should treat the lease and purchase commitments as fixed charges ahead of equity that the debt ratios do not capture.

No non-debt funding float is found: the filings state no material contract assets or liabilities and no supplier finance or factoring program appears in the sources read. Operating lease obligations of USD 612.1 million sit outside debt, and USD 163.4 million of letters of credit reduce revolver availability.
Basis: calculation C64; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 177; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51
### Definition and data-quality risks

Three debt totals coexist at 2026-09-30: USD 5,162.1 million on the balance sheet, which this module uses; USD 5,249.7 million of principal, which management uses; and USD 5,017.5 million in the fair-value table, which leaves out finance leases and other debt. The USD 144.6 million gap to the table cannot be itemised from the quarterly filing, so instrument-level carrying values are incomplete, and any covenant ratio would need the definitions in the credit agreement, which is not supplied.
Basis: calculation C58; calculation C59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 14

Ratios for FY2024 are not calculated because 2024 EBITDA contains Primo Water for seven weeks only, and net sales growth for 2025 is not comparable; the issuer's own comparable net sales basis for 2025 excludes USD 29.1 million of exited businesses, so reported growth of 2.61% for the first nine months of 2026 is not the issuer's comparable growth.

## Gaps

- The filings print a dash, which means nothing was reported, in 7 income statement cells, 36 cash flow cells and 3 balance sheet cells; each is written as not supplied rather than zero. No ratio uses these cells, so nothing is restricted. Severity Low. No action is needed unless the issuer confirms that a dash means nil.

- The annual report and the quarterly reports print different line sets, so 6 income statement cells, 78 cash flow cells and 9 balance sheet cells are not printed in the filing for that column; for example proceeds from the sale of property, plant and equipment become a separate line only from the second quarter of 2026 and the 2024 financing items do not recur. This limits line-by-line comparison across columns and nothing else. Severity Low. The action is to compare the subtotals, which are printed in every column.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_prmb-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-03-31_prmb-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 5

- Net Cash Change is withheld for FY2024, FY2025 and the first quarter, half year and nine months of 2025 because the printed net change includes the cash flows of discontinued operations, which the three activity rows exclude; the printed net change stays in the issuer's own row. This restricts only the cash roll-forward check for 2025. Severity Low. The action is to read the discontinued operations rows beside it.

- No filing after the annual report prints a debt maturity schedule, so the maturity chart is drawn at 2025-12-31 and still shows USD 3,005.7 million of term loans in 2028 that were extended to March 2031 on 2026-03-31. This restricts any maturity wall or refinancing-window statement as at the cutoff. Severity Medium. The action is to rebuild the post-amendment schedule from the term loan terms and label it derived.

- Instrument-level carrying values, finance leases, other debt and the total of unamortized costs are not stated at 2026-09-30, so the debt instruments register cannot reconcile to balance sheet debt and a gap of USD 144.6 million to the fair-value table stays unitemised; the year-end reconciliation is complete. This restricts instrument-level leverage and secured-debt statements at the cutoff. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the quarter's debt note or the issuer's schedule.
Basis: calculation C59; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92

- Management net debt and net leverage at 2025-12-31 are not printed in any source read, because the 2025 results release that carries them is not supplied; the three 2026 quarter-end figures are. This restricts a comparison of year-end leverage with management's own figure. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the 2025 results release.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86

- The credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so covenant definitions, any springing conditions on the revolver, and headroom against the first lien net leverage limit of 5.00 to 1.00 and the interest coverage minimum of 2.00 to 1.00 are not calculable; the issuer reports compliance only. This restricts any covenant or maturity-condition conclusion. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the executed agreements.

- The issuer does not state whether each add-back in Adjusted EBITDA is realised, and the bridge amounts reconcile exactly but their classification beyond the issuer's labels is not given. This restricts how far adjusted leverage can be relied on. Severity Medium. The action is to treat the add-backs as unverified and to seek the issuer's classification.

- Ranking is not stated for finance leases, other debt or the non-tendered original notes, and the revolver's security is stated only through the credit agreement description, so the first three are left out of the debt stack and the revolver is shown with that caveat. This restricts structural-priority statements. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the guarantee and security documents.

- The dividend declared on 2026-11-03 has no stated total, so the cash figure uses the share count of that date; the record-date count may differ. This restricts the pro forma net debt row slightly. Severity Low. The action is to replace it with the paid amount once reported.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39

- The 2025-09-30 balance sheet is not in a supplied filing, so no 2025 interim balance is shown beside the 2026 interim balances. This restricts the year-on-year comparison of debt and cash at interim dates. Severity Low. The action is none unless a third-quarter 2025 filing is added.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4

- Per-share data and share counts are not carried in the statement tables, because no credit metric uses them, and the single reporting segment means no segment schedule exists; revenue by water type is in the KPI dashboard instead. This restricts nothing in the ratios. Severity Low. No action is needed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183

Primo Brands Corp (issuer id prmb), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway: business, ownership, sponsor and governance facts, the 2024 merger and the debt issued or amended since 2025, from the seven supplied filings and news releases.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Primo Brands is a scaled single-segment water business whose main discretionary risk to creditors is shareholder payouts, and the sponsor's veto over them probably fell away in August 2026, leaving the board and the debt covenants as the only limits.
Basis: calculation C05; calculation C06; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47

Operations are not the weak point: net sales were USD 6,664.0 million in 2025 and management net leverage fell to 3.32x by 2026-09-30. Payouts are the exposure: 2025 dividends and buybacks of USD 572.8 million were 232.94% of free cash flow of USD 245.9 million, and a new USD 300.0 million buyback program followed on 2026-11-03.

Basis: calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C17; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 127–128; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62
### Key findings

Sponsor control is ending in steps, and the consent rights that let the sponsor restrain payouts most likely lapsed with the August 2026 sale. The sponsor group held 32.0% of the Class A shares on 2026-02-24, and its approval is required for dividends above USD 175.0 million a year, most repurchases and debt that takes total net leverage above 3.5x only while it holds at least 30%. The August 2026 sale and repurchase would leave it near 26.51%, an estimate that assumes those shares came from the group because no filing states the holding. If that holds, the board's own financial policy is the operative restraint on payouts.

Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C06; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

Company cash has been used to support the sponsor's exits, which is the clearest documented link between company liquidity and the sponsor since the merger. The company bought shares alongside all three sponsor offerings, USD 224.1 million in total, and 52.60% of the buybacks identified for 2025 were tied to sponsor sales; the company received none of the offering proceeds. Creditors bear this only through cash that is not used to repay debt.

Basis: calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 101–102; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58

Payout policy is the swing factor for leverage. In 2025 dividends and buybacks exceeded free cash flow by USD 326.9 million; in the first nine months of 2026 they took USD 201.3 million, or 62.98% of free cash flow of USD 319.6 million. Dividends declared for 2026 come to about USD 175.2 million, level with the USD 175.0 million consent threshold, and the new USD 300.0 million program was approved while management net leverage was 3.32x, under the 3.5x level in the sponsor's consent test, a level that management's own measure exceeded at 3.52x on 2026-03-31, although the agreement's definition may differ.

Basis: calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C34; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 127–128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–8; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62

The 2024 merger left a business judged on a short combined record with integration costs still running. Primo Water is consolidated only from 2024-11-09, goodwill is 70.03% of the USD 3,950.3 million purchase price, other integration expenses were USD 55.4 million in the first nine months of 2026, and a consumer class action alleges missed deliveries after facility closures and staff reductions. Earlier-period comparisons therefore mix a 2023 base that holds one of the two businesses with later periods that hold both.

The operating model is concentrated by product and customer rather than by segment, and 2026 growth is not yet turning into margin. Regional spring water and purified water were 49.82% and 31.54% of 2025 net sales, one customer was 21% of net sales, and premium water grew 31.66% in the first nine months of 2026; gross profit nevertheless fell by USD 22.6 million on net sales growth of 2.61% as transport and materials costs rose, and management guides 2026 Adjusted EBITDA to the lower end of its range.

Basis: calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C26; calculation C32; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2

Sponsor financing against the shares adds a forced-sale risk that sits outside the group's covenants. Almost all of the sponsor's shares, 99.95% of its 2026-02-24 holding by arithmetic on the stated pledges, back a margin loan and a prepaid variable share forward; a counterparty foreclosure could put shares on the market, and the credit agreement lists a change of control as an event of default and the 2029 unsecured notes carry a put at 101.0% of principal, with the definitions not supplied.
Basis: calculation C02; calculation C33; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 94–95; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99

Claims run through two co-issuing subsidiaries and a broad guarantor group, with the term loans and the secured notes sharing one first lien and the 2029 unsecured notes ranking below them; holders of original notes who did not exchange in 2025 lost most covenants on all three series and their guarantees on the two secured series, and USD 12.9 million of them remains. The March 2026 term loan refinancing moved the term loans from March 2028 to March 2031.

Basis: calculation C29; calculation C30; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 98; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30

Disclosure is adequate for monitoring but incomplete for control analysis. One person has been both Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman since November 2025, the exemption from independent-board rules ran to 2026-03-11, the 2026 proxy statement, which would show board independence and sponsor designee numbers, is not supplied, and the auditor gave an unqualified opinion with effective internal control at 2025-12-31. Litigation is real but unquantified: a securities class action with a motion to dismiss pending, a consumer class action on delivery service and a long-running label case.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a payout-risk view is that the sponsor may still hold at least 30%, because the 32.0% figure is rounded and the August 2026 shares may not all have come from the group; if so, the consent rights survive. Payouts also look affordable in 2026 at 62.98% of free cash flow, net leverage has fallen to 3.32x, the only distribution made to the sponsor alone, USD 448.6 million, pre-dates the merger, and none of the 2025 or 2026 refinancings is described as a priming, uptier or drop-down. The term loans described at 2025-12-31 also required prepayment from half of excess cash flow, subject to leverage step-downs, although the terms after the March 2026 amendment are not restated.

Basis: calculation C05; calculation C20; calculation C28; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

The view would soften if a filing or the proxy statement shows the sponsor at or above 30%, if payouts stay below free cash flow after the new program starts, and if net leverage keeps falling toward management's aim. It would harden if payouts exceed free cash flow again, if net leverage rises above 3.5x after buybacks begin, if the sponsor's margin loan or forward is enforced, or if any distribution is funded with new debt.
Basis: calculation C20; calculation C21; calculation C34; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47
### Limitations

- The executed Stockholders Agreement, credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so the consent thresholds, restricted-payment baskets and change-of-control definitions rest on the issuer's summaries; this limits the finding that payouts are restrained only by the board and the covenants, which could be stronger or weaker once the documents are read.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 78; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The sponsor's holding after August 2026 is not stated, so the 26.51% figure is derived on the assumption that the shares sold and repurchased came from the 32.0% group; this limits the conclusion that the veto rights lapsed, which is not established until a filing states the holding.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C05

- The 2026 proxy statement is not supplied, so the number of sponsor-designated directors, board independence, committee structure and pay are not established; this limits the governance finding to the officer list and the signatures, and it may change the view of how much control the sponsor retains.

- The sponsor's fund vintage, remaining fund life, entry price and equity contribution are not stated, so no exit pressure is inferred from the pattern of sell-downs; this limits the view of sponsor intent to documented actions only.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47

- Revenue by channel, customer concentration after 2025 and quantified merger synergies are not stated, so the operating view rests on the water-type mix and one 2025 customer figure; this limits how far margin recovery can be judged from the filings.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The 2024 merger created the issuer and its sponsor-controlled starting share register. On 2024-11-08 Primo Water Corporation and Triton Water Parent, Inc. (BlueTriton, the parent of the former Nestlé Waters North America business) became wholly owned subsidiaries of the new parent, Primo Brands Corporation. BlueTriton was the accounting acquirer, former Primo Water holders and the sponsor group owned about 43% and 57% immediately afterwards, and the USD 3,950.3 million purchase price was paid in shares and replacement awards, with goodwill of USD 2,766.5 million, 70.03% of the price. No cash sources and uses or entry multiple is stated.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 146–147; calculation C27

The 2025 refinancing replaced several instruments in one programme. Exchange offers for the three senior note series drew participation of 99.97%, 98.20% and 99.53%, and the new notes are co-issued by Primo Water Holdings Inc. and Triton Water Holdings, Inc. and guaranteed by the parent and substantially all material wholly owned domestic subsidiaries. On 2025-02-12 the Fourth Amendment repriced the term loans of USD 3,098.6 million principal and added a USD 750.0 million revolver maturing in February 2030, while a USD 350.0 million asset-based facility and Primo Water's prior revolver, which had an initial USD 350.0 million commitment, were repaid and ended. The new secured notes share the term loans' first lien and the 2029 unsecured notes rank below them; holders of original notes who did not tender lost most covenants on all three series and their guarantees on the two secured series, and USD 12.9 million of those notes remains.

On 2026-03-31 the Fifth Amendment refinanced the term loans of USD 3,067.6 million into USD 3,090.0 million maturing in March 2031, at SOFR plus 2.75% with a 0.50% floor and 1.00% a year of amortisation, a net principal increase of USD 22.4 million. This moved the term loan maturity out from March 2028; no maturity schedule printed after the amendment is supplied, so the next large maturities are taken to be the 2028 euro secured notes and the 2029 notes.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation C30

Equity transactions since the merger moved ownership rather than debt. The sponsor group sold down in three underwritten offerings priced at USD 29.50, USD 31.67 and USD 24.37 per share in 2025-03, 2025-05 and 2026-08, the company received none of the proceeds, and it bought shares alongside each for USD 224.1 million in total. On 2026-11-03 the board declared a dividend of USD 0.12 per share payable 2026-12-04 and approved a new USD 300.0 million repurchase program, both after the 2026-09-30 balance sheet.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 101–102; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C11

## Gaps

- The executed Stockholders Agreement, credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so the consent thresholds, restricted-payment baskets, change-of-control and unrestricted-subsidiary terms and covenant headroom rest on the issuer's summaries. This restricts any conclusion on how far payouts or new debt are limited. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the executed documents.

- The sponsor's holding after the August 2026 sale is not stated; the 26.51% figure assumes the shares sold and repurchased in that month came from the 32.0% group and is rounded. This restricts the conclusion that consent rights lapsed. Severity Medium. The action is to read the holding in the next filing or in the proxy statement.
Basis: calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

- The 2026 proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, the number of sponsor designees, committee composition, officer ownership and pay are not established. This restricts the governance view to officers and signatories. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the proxy statement.

- The sponsor's fund vintage, remaining life, entry price and equity contribution are not stated, and no exit pressure is inferred from vintage. This restricts any view of sponsor intent beyond documented actions. Severity Low. The action is to seek sponsor disclosures if the view is needed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47

- Revenue by channel, customer concentration after 2025 and quantified merger synergies are not stated in any supplied source. This restricts how far revenue durability and margin recovery can be judged. Severity Medium. The action is to seek channel and customer data from the issuer.

- The guarantor members and the subsidiary list (exhibit 21.1) are not supplied. This restricts structural priority statements to the issuer's description of the guarantor group. Severity Medium. The action is to obtain the exhibit and the indenture guarantor schedules.

- The funding source and date within 2024 of the USD 448.6 million sponsor dividend are not stated, and no filing links it to the USD 400.0 million incremental term loans of 2024-03-01. This restricts any conclusion that the distribution was debt funded. Severity Low. The action is to seek the pre-merger financing documents.
Basis: calculation C28; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93

- The businesses behind USD 48.0 million of acquisitions in the first nine months of 2026 and USD 29.0 million in 2025 are not described. This restricts any view of acquisition appetite. Severity Low. The action is to check the issuer's filings for the acquired businesses.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6

- Loss estimates are not given for the securities class action, the consumer class action or the label case, and the company states it cannot estimate a range. This restricts any view of contingent cash claims. Severity Medium. The action is to track rulings on the pending motions.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–37

- Open-market purchases by affiliated purchasers in the third quarter of 2026 are not identified. This restricts any view of insider alignment. Severity Low. The action is to check insider filings if needed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62

- The 2025 repurchase total in the cash flow statement, USD 421.5 million, exceeds the identified repurchases of USD 407.0 million by USD 14.5 million, and the nine-month 2026 total of USD 70.1 million exceeds the program figure of USD 66.6 million by USD 3.5 million; shares withheld for taxes are the likely cause but their value is not stated. This restricts the precision of the payout share tied to sponsor sales. Severity Low. The action is to use the stated figures as shown.
Basis: calculation C13; calculation C16; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18

spans.text: ## Request

Primo Brands Corp (issuer id prmb), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway: a fundamental credit view covering the business, financial profile, outlook, downside scenario and monitoring triggers, from the seven supplied filings and releases and the three supplied analyses.
## Sources

No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Primo Brands is an adequate credit whose improving leverage depends on shareholder payouts staying below free cash flow; creditors should treat financial policy, more than operations, as the swing factor.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C11; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Net debt was 3.87x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, or 3.91x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-03, against 4.51x at 2026-03-31; the gain came from earnings and cash rather than repayment, and 2026 margins are under cost pressure. Liquidity of USD 1,064.0 million, with pro forma cash after the dividend not established, and a term loan now due in 2031 leave the 2028 and 2029 notes of USD 1,930.1 million as the refinancing test.

Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C05; calculation C06; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51
### Key findings

The business profile is strong on scale and brand but narrow by product and customer. Net sales were USD 6,797.4 million over the last twelve months, spring water and purified water made up 81.36% of 2025 net sales, one customer was 21% of net sales, and the group runs one segment; scale and more than 80 spring sources, 36 company-owned, support cash-flow visibility, while the concentration means a pricing dispute or a service failure moves a large share of sales.

Basis: calculation C12; calculation C25; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 86

Leverage is falling but is high, and it rests on add-backs the issuer does not substantiate. Net debt of USD 4,684.7 million is 3.87x reported EBITDA (3.91x with the dividend declared on 2026-11-03, USD 4,728.1 million pro forma), against 3.26x on Adjusted EBITDA and the issuer's own 3.32x; the USD 227.0 million between the two EBITDA measures is 15.81% of Adjusted EBITDA. Since 2026-03-31 last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose by USD 130.4 million and cash by USD 189.2 million while gross debt rose by USD 6.8 million, so deleveraging came from earnings and cash build, not repayment.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C09; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 14

Margins, not sales, are the weak point of 2026. Nine-month net sales rose 2.61% but Adjusted EBITDA fell 0.96%, with a 10.4% fall in the first quarter followed by rises of 5.0% and 1.6%, and gross margin fell 1.22 percentage points, as the rise in transportation costs equalled 79.39% of the rise in net sales. Management cut the bottom of its Adjusted EBITDA range from USD 1,485 million to USD 1,465 million in May 2026 and now expects the lower end, which on the same definition needs fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 363.0 million, 8.65% above a year earlier and well above the best quarter so far.

Basis: calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 11; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 14

Cash conversion is improving but is flattered by the issuer's own adjusted measure. Free cash flow was USD 319.6 million in nine months 2026 against USD 203.4 million, 32.69% of reported EBITDA, but management's adjusted free cash flow of USD 602.9 million adds back USD 283.3 million of integration, restructuring and other items, USD 101.8 million of which is integration capital spending that rose from USD 84.5 million; payouts took 62.98% of free cash flow, leaving USD 118.3 million.
Basis: calculation C08; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C32; Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 12

Liquidity is adequate and the term loans no longer mature in 2028, but a sizeable note maturity and floating-rate cost remain. The 2028 euro secured notes and the 2029 secured and unsecured notes total USD 1,930.1 million, 38.47% of the instruments in the fair-value table and 1.81 times liquidity, and the term loans are 61.28% of them at SOFR plus 2.75%, so 100 bp adds USD 25.7 million a year today and USD 30.7 million once the USD 500.0 million of swaps have expired by 2027-12-31, against interest cover of 4.05x.

Basis: calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C18; calculation C19; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 101

Financial policy is the main constraint on the view. Payouts of USD 572.8 million in 2025 were 232.94% of free cash flow, the sponsor's holding is estimated at 26.51% after its August 2026 sale, which probably ended its consent rights over payouts and leverage, and a new USD 300.0 million buyback was approved on 2026-11-03; payouts in 2026 are lower, at 62.98% of free cash flow.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C17; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62

The primary downside path is cost inflation and service disruption lowering EBITDA while payouts continue. A 10% fall in last-twelve-months reported EBITDA would lift net leverage from 3.87x (3.91x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-03) to 4.31x and cut interest cover from 4.05x to 3.64x with net debt unchanged; the revolver's tests of 5.00x first lien net leverage and 2.00x interest cover are well clear of those levels on reported figures, but their definitions are not supplied.
Basis: calculation C04; calculation C20; calculation C21; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a better view is the speed of the improvement and the cash it produced: net leverage fell 0.64x in two quarters, interest cover is 4.05x against a 2.00x covenant minimum, premium water grew 31.66% and management says Direct Delivery returned to growth earlier than it anticipated. Payouts in 2026 are lower against free cash flow than in 2025, and the issuer's integration cash costs fell to USD 146.3 million from USD 206.2 million. If the add-backs prove one-off and margins recover with freight costs, the credit is stronger than adequate.

Basis: calculation C02; calculation C16; calculation C22; calculation C23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 12

The view would weaken if fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA falls short of the USD 363.0 million the guidance needs, if payouts exceed free cash flow again or net leverage on management's measure returns above 3.5x, or if the 2028 euro notes are not refinanced well before 2028-10-31. It would strengthen with filings showing sustained gross margin recovery, debt repayment from free cash flow, a printed maturity schedule after the 2026 amendment, or a sponsor stake confirmed at or above 30%, which would keep its consent rights over payouts in force.
Basis: calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C06; calculation C11; Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Limitations

- No maturity schedule or debt note after the 2026-03-31 term loan amendment is supplied, so the size of the 2028 and 2029 refinancing test rests on quarter-end carrying values; this limits the conclusion that the nearest maturities total USD 1,930.1 million, which could differ at principal.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; calculation C06

- The credit agreement's definitions of first lien net leverage and interest coverage are not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable; this limits the statement that reported ratios sit well inside the revolver tests to a comparison of stated levels with reported figures.

- No peer or sector benchmark is supplied, so the business profile is judged against the issuer's own history and statements; this limits the word adequate to issuer-level evidence and does not rank the credit against comparable issuers.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The issuer states no realisation status for its add-backs, so Adjusted EBITDA cannot be verified; this limits any conclusion that leverage is below 3.5x on an adjusted basis and keeps the view anchored on reported EBITDA.
Basis: calculation C03; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Fourth-quarter results, the 2026 dividend total and the pace of the new buyback are not yet known; this limits the payout conclusion to 2025 and nine months of 2026 and could move the 62.98% figure either way.
Basis: calculation C17; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Strengths and weaknesses

The strongest support is scale, brand and a spring-source network that spreads supply risk. Last-twelve-months net sales were USD 6,797.4 million from more than 50 production facilities and more than 80 spring sources, 36 company-owned, so one spring source failing does not stop supply, and the brand portfolio underpins pricing and cash-flow visibility; for creditors this absorbs shocks and underpins refinancing access.
Basis: calculation C25; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11

A second support is improving earnings and cash conversion. Free cash flow was USD 319.6 million in nine months 2026 against USD 203.4 million, up 57.13%, and reported EBITDA covered cash interest 4.05x against 3.57x for 2025, which lifts debt service capacity if the improvement holds.
Basis: calculation C04; calculation C16; Financial foundation (CP-1)

A third support is liquidity and an extended term loan. Cash and the undrawn revolver total USD 1,064.0 million at 2026-09-30, before the dividend declared on 2026-11-03 whose pro forma effect on cash is not established, the term loans now fall due in 2031 and the revolver in February 2030, so no large maturity falls before the euro notes due 2028-10-31.
Basis: calculation C05; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51

A fourth support is reporting quality and a record without priming. The auditor gave an unqualified opinion with effective internal control, quarterly reporting is regular, and the 2025 note exchange and 2026 term loan refinancing are not described as priming or uptier transactions, which supports monitoring and creditor alignment.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 122; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91

The most important weakness is financial policy under a falling sponsor stake. Payouts of USD 572.8 million in 2025 were 232.94% of free cash flow, USD 224.1 million of company cash was used beside the three sponsor sell-downs, and the estimated stake of 26.51% probably removed the sponsor's consent rights over payouts, so cash can leave faster than debt is repaid.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C26; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The second weakness is margin pressure that has stopped sales growth turning into EBITDA. Nine-month Adjusted EBITDA fell 0.96% on net sales up 2.61%, and transport cost growth equalled 79.39% of the sales increase, so deleveraging depends on a margin recovery that the lower end of the guidance already requires in the fourth quarter.
Basis: calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 11

The third weakness is leverage that rests on add-backs. Net debt is 3.87x reported EBITDA, or 3.91x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-03, and the USD 227.0 million of add-backs behind the lower adjusted figures is unverified, so creditors should underwrite to the reported measure.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The fourth weakness is concentration and service risk: spring water and purified water are 81.36% of sales, one customer is 21%, and a consumer class action alleges missed deliveries after facility closures, so one pricing or service failure can move a large share of sales and cash.
Basis: calculation C12; calculation C25; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36

The fifth weakness is refinancing and rate exposure: USD 1,930.1 million of notes fall due in 2028 and 2029, and the term loans are floating, so 100 bp adds USD 25.7 million a year today and USD 30.7 million once the swaps expire, while the revolver's springing maturity conditions are not printed.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C18; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26

### Business model and credit linkage

Primo Brands sells branded spring, purified, premium and refill water through retail, Direct Delivery, Exchange and Refill, formats that combine consumer retail demand with a recurring delivery and refill base. The recurring formats support cash-flow visibility, but Direct Delivery is also where integration problems surface: a consumer class action alleges missed deliveries after facility closures, and management says only that Direct Delivery returned to growth earlier than it anticipated, with no channel sales supplied. The creditor consequence is that visibility is good in the retail base and unproven in the delivery base.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 1
### Ownership and group structure

The issuer is a listed holding company whose notes are co-issued by two subsidiaries and guaranteed by the parent and substantially all material wholly owned domestic subsidiaries, with the term loans and secured notes sharing one first lien and the 2029 unsecured notes ranking below. The sponsor group held 32.0% at 2026-02-24 and is estimated at 26.51% after August 2026; sponsor-linked repurchases of USD 224.1 million, a quarterly dividend of USD 0.12 per share and USD 12.9 million of original notes that lost covenants and, on two series, guarantees show a financial policy that favours shareholders at the margin without any documented priming.

Basis: calculation C11; calculation C26; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 90–91; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 98; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99
### Revenue durability and pricing power

Revenue is largely a consumer staple with a recurring component, and the annual report states that cost increases have historically been recovered through price increases; 2026 tests that, because net sales grew 2.61% in nine months while the increase in transportation costs equalled 79.39% of it. Retail consolidation and private-label water cap pricing power, and one customer is 21% of net sales, so revenue is predictable in volume but not fully in price. Premium water, up 31.66%, is the one line growing fast enough to lift mix.

Basis: calculation C13; calculation C23; calculation C25; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22
### Cost structure and margin resilience

The cost base is commodity- and freight-linked: PET resin, aluminum, glass, fuel and energy, with the group bearing the risk and mitigating part through supplier pricing agreements and derivatives, and the filings do not split fixed from variable costs, so operating leverage is not measured. In nine months 2026 cost of sales rose by transportation costs of USD 105.9 million and materials costs of USD 33.0 million, and gross margin fell from 31.12% to 29.90%, so margins are defended mainly by pricing and productivity. Integration costs are fading, with other integration expenses of USD 55.4 million against USD 97.7 million, which helps reported EBITDA more than operating margin.

Basis: calculation C14; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital spending took 63.85% of operating cash flow in 2025 and 48.89% in nine months 2026, 6.52% and 5.83% of net sales, against base capital spending guided at 4% of net sales; the gap is mostly integration and disaster-related capital spending, USD 101.8 million of it integration in nine months, which should fall away as integration ends. Free cash flow converted 22.73% of reported EBITDA in 2025 and 32.69% in nine months 2026, and the group does not split maintenance from growth capital, so flexibility to cut capital spending in a downturn is real but not measured.

Basis: calculation C16; calculation C27; calculation C28; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_prmb-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 127–128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 12
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is high: national and regional beverage companies, retailer private labels and tap-water alternatives compete on brand, price and distribution, which limits price increases. New entry is limited by the cost of replicating a spring-source and depot network, which management calls difficult to replicate, while substitutes, from filtration to municipal water, cap the premium for bottled water. Buyer power is high because retail is consolidated and one customer is 21% of net sales, and supplier power is moderate because some packaging inputs come from few or sole suppliers; the credit effect is a margin ceiling that makes cost pass-through slower than cost inflation.
### External factors

External factors are a secondary credit driver on the provided materials, with three exceptions that are not quantified in the filings: local bans and taxes on plastic bottles and water extraction, tariff and freight cost pressure, and growing concern about contaminants in public water. They enter the monitoring triggers rather than the base view.
### Credit-translated SWOT

Credit strengths are scale, brands, spring-source redundancy, improving cash conversion and liquidity of USD 1,064.0 million at 2026-09-30. Credit weaknesses are leverage that depends on add-backs, margin pressure, concentration by product and customer, and payout policy. The opportunities that could improve credit quality are premium mix, the roll-off of integration costs and capital spending, and EBITDA growth that lowers leverage without repayment; the threats are freight and input cost inflation, plastic and water regulation, retailer pricing pressure, service-failure litigation and the sponsor's pledged shares.
Basis: calculation C05; calculation C23; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Financial profile and credit quality

The financial profile is adequate and improving. The main supports are scale, brands, liquidity of USD 1,064.0 million with pro forma cash after the 2026-11-03 dividend not established, interest cover of 4.05x and net leverage down to 3.87x, or 3.91x pro forma for that dividend. The main constraints are leverage that rests on USD 227.0 million of add-backs, margins that fell in 2026, payouts that took 232.94% of free cash flow in 2025, and a refinancing test of USD 1,930.1 million in 2028 and 2029. The trend is positive on cash and earnings, and the datapoints still missing are a post-amendment maturity schedule, covenant definitions and the sponsor's current holding.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C10; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

For the next 12 to 24 months the issuer guides to net sales growth of 2% to 4% and Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,465 million to USD 1,515 million, with Adjusted Free Cash Flow of USD 790 million to USD 810 million; the tailwinds are premium mix, Direct Delivery recovery and falling integration costs, and the headwinds are freight and input costs, a fourth-quarter EBITDA step of 8.65% that the guidance needs after the bottom of the range was cut from USD 1,485 million in May 2026, and floating-rate cost as the swaps expire. Over three to five years the credit depends on whether free cash flow goes to debt reduction, which is a policy choice that the sponsor's falling stake leaves to the board.
Basis: calculation C15; calculation C18; calculation C30; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 12

Sector tailwinds are that bottled water is the largest beverage category by volume and a USD 30 billion retail market in 2025, according to the annual report; sector headwinds are plastic regulation, retailer private labels and tariff and freight costs. Company tailwinds are the integration roll-off and a near-term maturity profile pushed to 2028; company headwinds are payout policy, customer concentration and litigation.
### Qualitative downside scenario

A realistic downside starts with a freight, resin and aluminum cost spike or a service failure in Direct Delivery that costs volume, while price increases lag. Revenue growth stalls, gross margin falls further from 29.90%, and EBITDA falls; a 10% fall in last-twelve-months reported EBITDA, with net debt unchanged, lifts net leverage from 3.87x (3.91x pro forma for the dividend declared on 2026-11-03) to 4.31x and cuts interest cover from 4.05x to 3.64x. Free cash flow falls more than EBITDA because interest and capital spending are largely fixed, and if payouts continue at the 2026 rate liquidity of USD 1,064.0 million at 2026-09-30 erodes while leverage stalls above 4x, so the 2028 and 2029 notes are refinanced from a weaker position.
Basis: calculation C05; calculation C14; calculation C20; Financial foundation (CP-1)

Management has levers: the new USD 300.0 million buyback is a ceiling and can be left unused, dividends can be cut from about USD 175.2 million a year, integration capital spending of USD 101.8 million in nine months should end, and base capital spending is guided at 4% of net sales. With those levers resilience looks sufficient to avoid a liquidity problem before 2028; default risk is not assumed from this evidence, and the first reading of stress would be a payout that exceeds free cash flow while net leverage on management's measure is above 3.5x.
Basis: calculation C17; calculation C21; calculation C27; calculation C29; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_prmb-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_ex991.htm.jsonl, page 12
### Overall credit view

Overall, Primo Brands presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, brands and a spring-source network, but credit quality is constrained by leverage that rests on add-backs, margin pressure in 2026 and a payout policy that the sponsor's falling stake no longer checks. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow rose to USD 319.6 million in nine months and interest cover is 4.05x, though adjusted free cash flow overstates it by USD 283.3 million. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA recovery and on payouts staying below free cash flow before the 2028 euro notes fall due on 2028-10-31, and the primary downside path is cost inflation and service disruption lowering EBITDA while payouts continue. Further analysis would require a printed maturity schedule, covenant definitions, the sponsor's current holding and fourth-quarter results. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: shareholder payouts outpacing free cash flow while margin pressure persists.
Basis: calculation C04; calculation C08; calculation C16; calculation C10; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
